+---
+depends_on:
+- 01M21AEPX6A1KRH0TQ0D4QV9CP

+position_ordinal: 9f80
+title: 'DiffView chrome: file list with counts, hunk actions, attach lines to prompt, hosting EditorKit''s diff view (plan §4.1, §9 C, §11#12)'
+---
+## What
+Create `Sources/AgentViewKit/Diff/DiffView.swift`, `DiffSummary.swift`, and `DiffRendererSlot.swift`, per plan.md §4.1 and decision 12.
+
+EditorKit's unified-diff view is specified in `../EditorKit/diff_plan.md` and does not exist yet. This task builds the kit's chrome against a `DiffRenderer` slot so it can ship before EditorKit does, and switches the default when EditorKit lands.
+
+- `DiffSummary.parse(gitPatch:) -> [FileSummary]` with path, operation, and added and removed counts, from the `+`, `-`, and header lines. A small parser, kept only for counts; the real parser is EditorKit's.
+- `DiffRendererSlot`: a `@ViewBuilder` slot `(patch: String, file: String?) -> View`. The default is `EditorKit.DiffView(patch:)` when the `EditorDiff` product is available, else a monospaced `Text` fallback that colors `+` and `-` lines. Use a compile-time check on the product import.
+- `DiffView(patch:)`: a per-file list with counts on the left (or on top when narrow), the renderer for the selected file, per-hunk Accept and Reject buttons that call host closures `onAccept(file, hunkIndex)` and `onReject`, and "Attach to prompt" that passes the selected lines to a host closure.
+- `ToolCallView` routes `ToolContent.diff` here.
+
+## Acceptance Criteria
+- [ ] `DiffSummary.parse` on a two-file patch gives two summaries with correct counts.
+- [ ] The file list selects the renderer's file.
+- [ ] Accept calls `onAccept` with the file and hunk index.
+- [ ] The fallback renderer shows added lines in the added color.
+
+## Tests
+- [ ] `Tests/AgentViewKitTests/Diff/DiffSummaryTests.swift`: counts on fixtures with add, delete, modify, and rename.
+- [ ] `Tests/AgentViewKitTests/Diff/DiffViewHostedTests.swift`: selection and the action closures.
+- [ ] `swift test --filter AgentViewKitTests` exits 0.
+
+## Workflow
+- Use `/tdd` — write failing tests first, then implement to make them pass.
\ No newline at end of file
